```go
func verifyMiosaSignature(body []byte, header, secret string) bool {
    parts := map[string]string{}
    for _, part := range strings.Split(header, ",") {
        kv := strings.SplitN(part, "=", 2)
        if len(kv) == 2 {
            parts[kv[0]] = kv[1]
        }
    }
    ts, ok1 := parts["t"]
    received, ok2 := parts["v1"]
    if !ok1 || !ok2 {
        return false
    }

    tsInt, err := strconv.ParseInt(ts, 10, 64)
    if err != nil || math.Abs(float64(time.Now().Unix()-tsInt)) > 300 {
        return false
    }

    signed := fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ts, string(body))
    mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(secret))
    mac.Write([]byte(signed))
    expected := hex.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))

    return hmac.Equal([]byte(expected), []byte(received))
}

func webhookHandler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    body, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
    sig := r.Header.Get("Miosa-Signature")

    if !verifyMiosaSignature(body, sig, webhookSecret) {
        http.Error(w, "invalid signature", http.StatusUnauthorized)
        return
    }

    // parse and handle body ...
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
}
```

---

## Idempotency

MIOSA may deliver the same event more than once (network retries, at-least-once semantics). Make your handler idempotent by storing the event `id` and discarding duplicates:

```python
processed_events = set()  # use a database or cache in production

def handle_event(event: dict) -> None:
    event_id = event["id"]
    if event_id in processed_events:
        return  # duplicate  -  skip
    processed_events.add(event_id)

    match event["type"]:
        case "sandbox.running":
            notify_user(event["data"]["external_user_id"])
        case "sandbox.destroyed":
            release_resources(event["data"]["id"])
        case "sandbox.error":
            alert_oncall(event["data"])
```

---

## Retry policy

| Attempt | Delay |
|---|---|
| 1 (initial) | Immediate |
| 2 | 1 minute |
| 3 | 5 minutes |
| 4 | 30 minutes |
| 5 | 1 hour |
| 6 | 2 hours |
| 7 | 4 hours |
| 8 | 8 hours |

MIOSA makes up to eight delivery attempts over roughly 15.5 hours (within a 24-hour window), then drops the event. If your endpoint is unreachable, check the webhook delivery log in the MIOSA dashboard.

Return a `2xx` status code within **10 seconds** to acknowledge receipt. If your processing takes longer, acknowledge immediately and handle the event asynchronously.

---

## Register a webhook

**Python**

```python
hook = client.webhooks.create(
    url="https://example.com/webhooks/miosa",
    events=[
        "sandbox.created",
        "sandbox.running",
        "sandbox.paused",
        "sandbox.destroyed",
        "sandbox.error",
    ],
    description="Lumen lifecycle events",
)

# The secret is returned only on creation. Store it immediately.
print(hook["secret"])  # MIOSA_WEBHOOK_SECRET=...
```

**TypeScript**

```typescript
const hook = await client.webhooks.create({
  url: "https://example.com/webhooks/miosa",
  events: [
    "sandbox.created",
    "sandbox.running",
    "sandbox.paused",
    "sandbox.destroyed",
    "sandbox.error",
  ],
  description: "Lumen lifecycle events",
});

// The secret is returned only on creation. Store it immediately.
console.log(hook.secret); // MIOSA_WEBHOOK_SECRET=...
```

> **Caution: Copy the secret now**
>
> The webhook secret is returned once at creation. If you lose it, delete the webhook and create a new one.

---

## Local testing

Use a tunnel to expose your local server during development:

```bash
# Option 1  -  ngrok
ngrok http 8000
# Copy the https URL, set MIOSA_WEBHOOK_URL in .env

# Option 2  -  cloudflared
cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000
```

Then run the one-time setup script to register the tunnel URL as your webhook endpoint. When you restart the tunnel and get a new URL, update the webhook:

```python
# Update an existing webhook's URL
client.webhooks.update("whk_abc123", url="https://new-tunnel.ngrok.io/webhooks/miosa")
```

---

- [Preview Tokens](/docs/develop/previews)
- [Sandbox API reference](/docs/api-reference/sandboxes)

pages.title: Agent credit metering
pages.description: How to meter credits for MIOSA agent runs, model usage, devices, tools, storage, and deployments.
pages.markdown:
Credits are the business model for agent work on MIOSA. A user does not buy
"a sandbox" or "a model call" in isolation. They buy credits that power agents
doing useful work on devices.

```text
credits = model usage + device runtime + tools + storage + deployments
```

Use this page when building billing, quotas, usage pages, workspace budgets,
or white-label credit systems.

---

## Metered surfaces

| Surface | Examples | When charged |
|---|---|---|
| Model/runtime | OSA, Codex, Claude Code, Hermes, custom model calls | During agent reasoning and tool planning |
| Sandbox runtime | CPU/RAM while sandbox is running | While executing, previewing, installing, building |
| Computer runtime | Cloud desktop/browser time | While browser/desktop session is active |
| Local relay | Secure relay, streaming, tunnel, control channel | While paired local device is connected through MIOSA |
| Tool calls | Browser actions, web search, Refero, connector token requests | Per call or per run allocation |
| Storage | Snapshots, artifacts, logs, persistent files | By size and retention |
| Deploy hosting | MIOSA Deploy, Docker Host, domains, always-on app runtime | While deployed or always-on |

> **Note: One ledger**
>
> Even if each subsystem records internal metrics, customer-visible billing should
> land in one credit ledger with workspace, user, run, agent, and device context.

---

## Ledger shape

```sql
credit_ledger
  id
  tenant_id
  workspace_id
  project_id
  user_id
  agent_id
  run_id
  device_type
  device_id
  category
  units
  unit_price_credits
  credits
  metadata_json
  created_at
```

Recommended categories:

```text
model
device_runtime
tool
connector
storage
deployment
network
adjustment
grant
refund
```

Each ledger entry should be traceable to a run, request id, or lifecycle event.

---

## Run-level cost model

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  P[Prompt] --> M[Model usage]
  P --> D[Device runtime]
  P --> T[Tools/connectors]
  P --> S[Storage/artifacts]
  P --> H[Deploy/hosting]
  M --> C[Credit ledger]
  D --> C
  T --> C
  S --> C
  H --> C
```

Every agent run should expose:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `estimated_credits` | Show before high-cost work starts |
| `reserved_credits` | Prevent a run from exceeding budget mid-flight |
| `credits_used` | Final charge |
| `credit_breakdown` | Explain model/device/tool/storage/deploy split |
| `budget_remaining` | Let UI warn before next action |

---

## Simple examples

### One-shot health check

```text
User runs: miosa run "check preview"

Charges:
  model: small
  device_runtime: seconds
  storage: none
  deploy: none
```

### Sandbox app generation

```text
User asks: "Build a Next.js marketing page."

Charges:
  model: planning and code generation
  sandbox_runtime: install, build, preview
  storage: files, logs, snapshot
  deployment: only if user publishes
```

### Browser automation

```text
User asks: "Log in and test checkout."

Charges:
  model: browser planning
  computer_runtime: browser session
  tool: screenshots and browser actions
  storage: screenshots/report artifact
```

### Agent-company workflow

```text
User asks: "Launch this company campaign."

Charges:
  parent model run
  child model runs
  multiple sandboxes/computers
  connectors
  artifacts
  optional deployment
```

---

## Budget policies

Workspace owners should be able to set:

- monthly credit budget
- per-run max credits
- per-agent daily budget
- max concurrent sandboxes
- max concurrent computers
- max child agents
- max connector spend
- approval threshold
- hard stop threshold

Recommended approval gates:

| Action | Gate |
|---|---|
| Use more than run budget | Ask approval |
| Create many child devices | Ask approval |
| Start always-on deployment | Ask approval |
| Use paid connector | Ask approval or preconfigured policy |
| Send external messages | Ask approval |
| Delete snapshots/artifacts | Ask approval |

---

## Credits in white-label products

White-label products can expose credits in two ways:

| Model | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Pass-through | End customer sees MIOSA credit usage directly |
| Wrapped | Your product shows its own units, while backend maps to MIOSA credits |

For Lumen-style products, the backend should store both:

```sql
customer_usage_events
  external_workspace_id
  external_user_id
  external_project_id
  miosa_run_id
  miosa_credits
  customer_units
```

This lets your app show the product-specific balance while still reconciling to
MIOSA billing.

---

## Credit events

Emit events so the UI can update live:

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `credits.estimated` | Before a run, publish, or expensive connector action |
| `credits.reserved` | Budget held for a run |
| `credits.charged` | Ledger entry committed |
| `credits.refunded` | Failed or cancelled work refunded |
| `credits.low_balance` | Workspace balance below threshold |
| `credits.limit_reached` | Run blocked by plan or budget |

The CLI should report the same data:

```bash
miosa billing balance
miosa workspace usage <slug>
miosa run usage <run-id>
miosa whoami --json
```

---

## Failure handling

Billing should be conservative and explainable.

| Failure | Expected billing behavior |
|---|---|
| Run rejected before start | No charge |
| Device created but agent failed before work | Charge minimal device time or refund per policy |
| Upload/import failed after resource creation | Return partial resource id and recovery command |
| User cancels | Charge work already performed, stop future charging |
| Platform error | Refund affected usage where possible |
| Connector/provider error | Charge only completed provider work |

Always include request ids and run ids in billing-support views.

---

## See also

- [Usage and billing](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing): Workspace billing, plan limits, and platform usage surfaces.
- [Agent product model](/docs/guides/agent-product-model): The product primitives that credits meter.
- [Agent workflow patterns](/docs/guides/agent-workflow-patterns): How different workflows consume credits.
- [API reference: usage rollup](/docs/api-reference/usage-rollup): Query usage summaries for dashboards and reports.

pages.title: Build a virtual-device product
pages.description: Build a Nebula-style product on MIOSA with persistent devices, files, browser work, jobs, artifacts, and connected tools.
pages.markdown:
A virtual-device product gives users and agents a shared machine that keeps
state between conversations. It can hold files, run code, keep browser context,
execute jobs, connect to apps, and produce artifacts.

This is the MIOSA pattern behind Nebula-style devices, always-on operators,
agent workspaces, browser automation products, and AI company workrooms.

---

## Product promise

```text
"Give each workspace a persistent device where agents can work, remember files,
run apps, use a browser, and continue later."
```

The user should experience:

- a workspace device that does not disappear after a short timeout
- visible files and generated artifacts
- a browser or preview panel
- resumable agent sessions
- jobs that can run in the background
- connected tools and credentials
- clear usage and credits
- safe approval prompts

---

## MIOSA mapping

| Virtual-device concept | MIOSA primitive |
|---|---|
| Device | Sandbox or computer |
| Files between sessions | Persistent `/workspace`, computer storage, snapshots |
| Browser | Computer browser or browser-capable runtime |
| Code | Sandbox exec and files |
| Live server | Sandbox preview ports |
| Jobs | Scheduled agent runs that resume a device |
| Shared workspace | Workspace-scoped device policy |
| Connected apps | Managed connectors and secrets |
| Outputs | Artifacts, previews, deployments |
| Billing | Credit ledger by run/device/tool/storage |

---

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  UI[Product UI] --> API[Your backend]
  API --> DB[(Your DB)]
  API --> S[Primary sandbox]
  API --> C[Optional computer]
  API --> J[Job queue]
  J --> A[Agent runtime]
  A --> S
  A --> C
  S --> Art[Artifacts and previews]
  C --> Shot[Screenshots and browser state]
  Art --> UI
  Shot --> UI
```

The product owns device assignment and policy. MIOSA owns the execution layer.

---

## Data model

```sql
workspaces
  id
  primary_device_type
  primary_device_id
  credit_budget

workspace_devices
  id
  workspace_id
  miosa_device_type
  miosa_device_id
  name
  role
  status
  persistent
  latest_snapshot_id
  created_at
  updated_at

agent_sessions
  id
  workspace_id
  device_id
  runtime
  status
  last_prompt
  created_at
  updated_at

workspace_artifacts
  id
  workspace_id
  session_id
  path
  content_type
  preview_url
  download_url
  version
```

---

## Device lifecycle

Use persistent devices by default for interactive work.

```text
create workspace
  -> create primary sandbox
  -> install starter runtime/tools
  -> save first snapshot
  -> mark device ready

user sends prompt
  -> resume primary device
  -> start agent run
  -> stream events
  -> snapshot stable checkpoint

idle timeout
  -> stop compute
  -> preserve filesystem
  -> device remains resumable
```

Destroy should be explicit. Timeout should stop compute and preserve state for
normal workspaces.

> **Note: Do not make active work disposable by default**
>
> For agent-building workflows, short destroy timeouts break trust. Use
> persistence, snapshots, idle warnings, and explicit delete semantics.

---

## UI layout

Recommended panes:

| Pane | Shows |
|---|---|
| Chat/task | User prompts and assistant messages |
| Activity | Tool calls, command output, browser actions |
| Files | Workspace file tree and changed files |
| Preview/browser | Live server or computer stream |
| Artifacts | Downloadable outputs and versions |
| Jobs | Scheduled and running background work |
| Credits | Current balance and run cost |
| Approvals | Risky actions waiting for user confirmation |

The activity pane should show the work as it happens. If the agent writes code,
the user should see file changes and commands. If it uses a browser, the user
should see screenshots or stream events.

---

## CLI shape

Developers should be able to operate the same product from CLI:

```bash
miosa create company-workspace --template nextjs --wait
miosa device list

miosa agent run builder \
  --sandbox company-workspace \
  --no-follow

miosa run events <run-id>
miosa run files <run-id>
```

For browser work:

```bash
miosa computer create browser-qa --template miosa-desktop
miosa agent run builder \
  --computer browser-qa \
  --no-follow
```

---

## Jobs and schedules

Virtual-device products become powerful when agents can keep working.

Examples:

- daily competitor research
- weekly app QA
- CRM enrichment
- support inbox triage
- website uptime checks
- automated report generation
- recurring content drafts

Job model:

```sql
agent_jobs
  id
  workspace_id
  agent_id
  device_id
  schedule
  prompt_template
  status
  next_run_at
  budget_limit
```

Jobs should resume the assigned device, run the prompt, stream events, save
artifacts, and stop the device when idle.

---

## Connected tools

Connectors turn the device into a useful worker:

| Connector | Use |
|---|---|
| GitHub | Issues, PRs, repo context, code review |
| Slack | Notifications, summaries, approval requests |
| Google Drive | Source docs and generated files |
| Gmail | Drafts and inbox triage with approval |
| Refero | Design research and product UI references |
| Custom API key | Customer's own provider or SaaS API |

Connector tokens should be scoped to the workspace and action. The agent should
not receive tenant admin keys unless that is explicitly allowed.

---

## Safety defaults

Require approval for:

- external messages
- production deploys
- high-cost device creation
- large fleet runs
- deleting files, snapshots, devices, or deployments
- using admin credentials
- buying domains or paid resources

Always log:

- who asked
- which agent acted
- which device executed
- which connector was used
- what changed
- what credits were charged

---

## Build checklist

1. Create a workspace record.
2. Create a persistent primary sandbox.
3. Store the MIOSA sandbox id.
4. Add a visible files/artifacts pane.
5. Add a run event stream.
6. Add `agent start`, `agent task`, and `agent events` paths.
7. Add connector settings.
8. Add approval gates.
9. Add credit metering.
10. Add snapshots and resume.
11. Add optional computer for browser work.
12. Add deploy/publish path.

---

## See also

- [Agent devices](/docs/guides/agent-devices): Sandboxes, computers, local devices, persistence, and primary device policy.
- [Agent workflow patterns](/docs/guides/agent-workflow-patterns): Pick the right workflow from one-shot prompt to agent fleet.
- [Agent credit metering](/docs/platform/agent-credit-metering): Meter model, device, tool, storage, and deployment usage.
- [Build an agent-company platform](/docs/guides/build-agent-company): Extend virtual devices into department agents and company operators.

pages.title: UI Components
pages.description: Drop-in React, Vue, and Svelte components for embedding MIOSA sandboxes in your own frontend.
pages.markdown:
`@miosa/react`, `@miosa/vue`, and `@miosa/svelte` are drop-in component libraries that let you embed live MIOSA sandboxes directly in your own frontend  -  no iframe glue code, no WebSocket wiring, no API plumbing.

Each package ships four production-ready components:

| Component | What it renders |
|---|---|
| `<MiosaPreview>` | A sandboxed iframe showing your sandbox's HTTP preview URL |
| `<MiosaTerminal>` | A full xterm.js terminal connected to a sandbox PTY over WebSocket |
| `<MiosaFileTree>` | An interactive file browser backed by the sandbox filesystem |
| `<MiosaUsage>` | A usage summary widget (compute seconds, storage, egress) per end-user |

These are the customer-facing drop-in packages: your app imports them to embed a sandbox in your own frontend. They are separate from the MIOSA Foundation component library, which is the internal UI system for building the MIOSA product itself. Use [Foundation Component Library](/docs/component-library) for the product UI system, design tokens, cleanup rules, and reusable internal components.

## Auth model

> **Caution: Never put API keys in the browser**
>
> Your MIOSA API key (`msk_*`) must stay on your server. Components that accept an `apiKey` prop are intended for **server-rendered** or **trusted-client** contexts only. For public-facing embeds, generate a short-lived preview token on your backend and pass it as `previewToken`.

The recommended pattern for public embeds:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Browser
    participant YourBackend
    participant MiosaAPI as api.miosa.ai

    Browser->>YourBackend: GET /sandbox-token?sandboxId=sb_...
    YourBackend->>MiosaAPI: POST /api/v1/sandboxes/{id}/preview-token
    Note over YourBackend,MiosaAPI: Uses msk_* API key  -  server only
    MiosaAPI-->>YourBackend: { token, expires_at }
    YourBackend-->>Browser: { token }
    Browser->>Browser: <MiosaPreview previewToken={token} />
```

`<MiosaPreview>` and `<MiosaTerminal>` both accept a `previewToken` in place of an `apiKey`. Tokens are short-lived (1 hour by default) and scoped to a single sandbox.

## Which framework package to choose

| If you use... | Install |
|---|---|
| React / Next.js / Remix | `@miosa/react` |
| Vue 3 / Nuxt 3 | `@miosa/vue` |
| Svelte 5 / SvelteKit | `@miosa/svelte` |

The component APIs are structurally identical across all three packages. Prop names, event names, and behavior are the same  -  only the import path and framework idioms differ.

## Install

**React**

```bash
npm install @miosa/react
# xterm peer deps  -  required only if you use MiosaTerminal
npm install @xterm/xterm @xterm/addon-fit
```

**Vue**

```bash
npm install @miosa/vue
# xterm peer deps  -  required only if you use MiosaTerminal
npm install @xterm/xterm xterm-addon-fit
```

**Svelte**

```bash
npm install @miosa/svelte
# xterm peer deps  -  required only if you use MiosaTerminal
npm install @xterm/xterm xterm-addon-fit
```

Also add the stylesheet to your app entry point (React only  -  Vue and Svelte bundle their own scoped styles):

```ts
import '@miosa/react/styles.css';
```

## See also

- [Foundation Component Library](/docs/component-library)
- [React components](/docs/ui-components/react)
- [Vue components](/docs/ui-components/vue)
- [Svelte components](/docs/ui-components/svelte)
- [Platform: Browser Tokens](/docs/platform/browser-tokens)
- [Sandbox previews](/docs/develop/previews)

pages.title: Foundation UI
pages.description: The owned MIOSA frontend primitives used by the platform application.
pages.markdown:
The MIOSA platform owns a Foundation UI primitive set exposed to the Svelte app through the `$foundation` alias.

Use this surface for platform screens before adding route-local buttons, inputs, cards, modals, tabs, tables, or page chrome.

## Owned primitive surface

| Primitive group | Components |
|---|---|
| Actions | `Button`, `PillButton` |
| Forms | `Input`, `RoundedInput`, `Textarea`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, `Toggle`, `RadioGroup`, `Slider` |
| Layout | `GlassCard`, `AppCard`, `Separator`, `ScrollArea`, `Breadcrumb` |
| Feedback | `Alert`, `Toast`, `Loading`, `Skeleton`, `Progress` |
| Overlays | `Modal`, `Popover`, `Tooltip`, `Menu` |
| Data display | `Table`, `Tabs`, `Accordion`, `Avatar` |

## Import path

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { GlassCard, PillButton, Alert, Table } from "$foundation";
</script>
```

The alias is configured in the platform Svelte config and resolves to:

```text
src/lib/foundations-components/src/lib/ui
```

## Compute workspace audit

The Compute workspace was using this surface inconsistently. Shared Compute components often use `$foundation`, but several top-level Compute routes still hand-roll controls, tables, cards, and page shells with route-local CSS.

| Route | Current state |
|---|---|
| Projects | Mostly shared Compute components; low direct Foundation usage in the page. |
| Deploy | High custom UI; raw filters, buttons, selects, table, and route CSS remain. |
| Logs | Partial Foundation usage through `PillButton`; raw inputs and table remain. |
| Analytics | Visible cards and actions converted to `GlassCard` and `PillButton`. |
| Environment Variables | Partial Foundation usage through `PillButton`; raw modal, form, and table remain. |
| Domains | Partial Foundation usage through `PillButton`; raw modal and table remain. |
| Storage | High custom UI; raw tabs, search, buttons, card grid, and route CSS remain. |
| Databases | Partial Foundation usage through `PillButton`; raw cards and modal remain. |
| Sandboxes | Partial Foundation usage through `PillButton`; raw table and filter controls remain. |
| Computers | Partial Foundation usage through `PillButton`; raw table and filter controls remain. |

## Cleanup order

1. Convert route-level actions and empty/error states to `PillButton`, `Alert`, `Skeleton`, and shared empty-state components.
2. Replace raw form controls with `RoundedInput`, `Input`, `Select`, `Checkbox`, and `Toggle`.
3. Replace hand-rolled tabs and chips with `Tabs` or a shared Compute filter-chip component.
4. Replace raw tables and cards with Foundation table primitives or shared Compute table/card components.
5. Collapse repeated shell CSS into shared Compute layout primitives instead of copying page, console, and main CSS per route.

## Verification guardrail

Every migrated route should keep passing:

```bash
pnpm check
pnpm test:e2e tests/platform-shell-regression.spec.ts --project=chromium
pnpm build
```

## See also

- [UI Components overview](/docs/ui-components)
- [React components](/docs/ui-components/react)
- [Vue components](/docs/ui-components/vue)
- [Svelte components](/docs/ui-components/svelte)

`@miosa/vue` v0.3.2 provides four Vue 3 single-file components for embedding MIOSA sandboxes. All components are written with ` ``` ### Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `sandboxId` | `string` | - | **Required.** The sandbox ID to preview. | | `previewToken` | `string` | - | Short-lived preview token from your backend. Mutually exclusive with `apiKey`. | | `apiKey` | `string` | - | Your MIOSA API key. Use only in trusted server-rendered contexts. | | `theme` | `"light" \| "dark"` | `"light"` | Visual theme. | | `class` | `string` | - | Forwarded to the root `
`. | ### Events | Event | Payload | Description | |---|---|---| | `error` | `Error` | Emitted when the preview URL cannot be resolved. | Exactly one of `previewToken` or `apiKey` must be provided. --- ## MiosaTerminal Renders a full PTY terminal connected to a sandbox over WebSocket, powered by xterm.js. > **Caution** > > `MiosaTerminal` requires `apiKey`. Keep it in server-rendered or internal tooling pages - do not expose your API key in public client-side code. ```vue ``` ### Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `sandboxId` | `string` | - | **Required.** | | `apiKey` | `string` | - | **Required.** | | `theme` | `"light" \| "dark"` | `"dark"` | Sets the xterm.js color scheme. | ### Events | Event | Payload | Description | |---|---|---| | `resize` | `[cols: number, rows: number]` | Emitted when the terminal dimensions change. | | `error` | `Error` | Emitted on WebSocket errors or xterm load failure. | The component auto-fits to its container via `ResizeObserver` and syncs resize events to the PTY. --- ## MiosaFileTree Renders a flat-list file browser backed by the sandbox filesystem. Directories expand inline on click; files emit a `select` event. ```vue ``` ### Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `sandboxId` | `string` | - | **Required.** | | `apiKey` | `string` | - | **Required.** | | `showHidden` | `boolean` | `false` | Include dotfiles and hidden directories. | | `defaultExpanded` | `boolean` | `false` | When `true`, all directories start expanded. | ### Events | Event | Payload | Description | |---|---|---| | `select` | `path: string` | Emitted when a file is clicked. `path` is the absolute path within the sandbox (e.g. `/workspace/src/index.ts`). | | `change` | `[path: string, type: "created" \| "deleted" \| "modified"]` | Emitted on filesystem changes (when the watch subscription fires). | --- ## MiosaUsage Renders a three-column usage summary (compute, storage, egress) for a specific end-user. ```vue ``` ### Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---| | `externalUserId` | `string` | - | **Required.** Your platform's user ID, matching the `external_user_id` used when creating sandboxes. | | `apiKey` | `string` | - | **Required.** | | `period` | `"current" \| "last_30" \| "last_7"` | `"current"` | Billing period to aggregate over. `"current"` is the current billing cycle; `"last_30"` / `"last_7"` are rolling day windows. | | `theme` | `"light" \| "dark"` | `"light"` | Visual theme. | Displays `compute_seconds`, `storage_gb_hours`, and `egress_gb`. No events are emitted. --- ## End-to-end example: Nuxt 3 **`server/api/sandbox-token.post.ts`** - server route (keeps API key off the client) ```ts import Miosa from '@miosa/sdk'; export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => { const { sandboxId } = await readBody<{ sandboxId: string }>(event); const client = new Miosa({ apiKey: process.env.MIOSA_API_KEY! }); const sandbox = await client.sandboxes.get(sandboxId); // @ts-expect-error const { token } = await sandbox.previewToken(3600); return { token }; }); ``` **`pages/workbench.vue`** ```vue ``` > **Tip** > > In Nuxt 3, use `runtimeConfig` to expose the API key only on the server side (`runtimeConfig.miosaApiKey`, not `runtimeConfig.public.miosaApiKey`). This prevents it from being serialized into the client bundle. ## See also - [UI Components overview](/docs/ui-components) - [Platform: Browser Tokens](/docs/platform/browser-tokens) - [React components](/docs/ui-components/react) - [Svelte components](/docs/ui-components/svelte)

pages.title: Build an app like...
pages.description: Guides for platform builders. Run open-source agents and frameworks on MIOSA, or build familiar AI products like Lovable, Manus and Perplexity - app builders, coding agents, autonomous and computer-use agents, chat and companions, answer engines, multi-agent, voice, design, video, vertical apps, and an internal Business OS.
pages.markdown:
Build

Product shapes people already know, mapped onto MIOSA primitives. Build any of them for your own company or as a product for your customers, on the same architecture. Each guide is one page: what it is, the resources you need, an architecture diagram, six steps you can run, and an agent prompt for your coding agent.

[Compare MIOSA](/docs/compare)[Platform builder guide](/docs/platform/overview)[Sandboxes](/docs/develop/sandboxes)[Deploy and Docker Host](/docs/docker-host/overview)

Every guide is one of two kinds:

- **Run X on MIOSA.** Open-source agents, frameworks and tools you can actually install and use (OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor's CLI agent, CrewAI, AutoGen, LangGraph, Pipecat, Browser Use, Stagehand, Steel). The guide and its agent prompt install the real tool from its official docs, run it on a MIOSA sandbox or computer, and then wrap it for your team or your customers.
- **Build an app like X.** Closed products you cannot run yourself (Lovable, Bolt, v0, Manus, Perplexity, Character.AI and others). The guide names the product, maps each of its capabilities onto a MIOSA primitive, and builds your own version.

Either kind can be set up **two ways, on the same architecture**:

- **For your own company (internal).** One organization, a workspace per team, access control and SSO, and an internal domain. No billing.
- **As a product (for your customers).** Multi-tenant: white-label branding, an organization or workspace per customer, custom domains, and usage metering.

Each guide ships an **agent prompt tailored to what you are building** - pick the shape and a name, and hand the brief to OSA, Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor. Browse the apps and platforms below.

MIOSA is the execution layer underneath AI products. The core idea runs through every guide:
**build your product powered by Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, OpenClaw, OSA, or your own model**.
The harness runs inside a MIOSA sandbox or computer, and your product wraps it.

There are two paths, and they are not exclusive:

- [Run the agents as-is, for your team](/docs/build/run-agents): Background coding agents, parallel sessions per sandbox, and a persistent workspace per developer. No product to build: just run Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or your own harness in the cloud and watch the work.
- [Build a branded product on top](/docs/build/coding-agent-product): Wrap a harness in your own UI, model, and billing: a Lovable-style builder, an internal workspace, or a customer-facing product, using Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, or your own model under the hood.

## Ideas to build

- [Your own Claude-desktop-style app](/docs/build/claude-cowork): A branded desktop/web app where your users chat with an agent that works in its own cloud computer, with a browser and files.
- [Artifacts with links](/docs/build/lovable): The agent builds something (a site, a doc, a dashboard, or an app), shares it at a preview URL, then promotes it to a deployment on your own branded domain.
- [An internal AI workspace](/docs/build/business-os): An Acme Corp-style internal platform: one place for your team's agents, apps, and data, behind your own login.
- [A customer-facing product](/docs/platform/white-label): The same shape, Lumen-style and white-label: your brand, your domains, and your end users, with MIOSA running behind them.
- [Run coding agents in the cloud](/docs/build/run-agents): Put Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor agents in sandboxes: background work, parallel sessions, and a persistent workspace each.
- [A multi-agent team](/docs/build/openswarm): An orchestrator that fans work out to child agents in their own machines and joins the results.

### AI app builders

Prompt to a running, previewable, deployable app.

- [Build a Lovable-style app Prompt a full-stack app, preview it live, publish it.](/docs/build/lovable)
- [Build a Bolt-style app Full-stack apps from a prompt, on a real dev server.](/docs/build/bolt)
- [Build a v0-style app Generate a UI from a prompt and publish it.](/docs/build/v0)
- [Build a Replit-Agent-style app A cloud workspace where a prompt becomes a running app.](/docs/build/replit)
- [Build a Base44-style app Describe an app, get a working, previewed one.](/docs/build/base44)
- [Build an Emergent-style app Prompts become running software with real infrastructure.](/docs/build/emergent)
- [Build a Rork-style app Prompt to a mobile app you can preview.](/docs/build/rork)
- [Build an Anything-style app Prompt to a working web or mobile app.](/docs/build/anything)

### Run coding agents

Install Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline and OpenHands on MIOSA, or build a product on them.

- [Run coding agents in the cloud Claude Code, Codex, Cursor: background agents in the cloud.](/docs/build/run-agents)
- [Run Claude Code on MIOSA Install it in a sandbox; stream and collect its work.](/docs/build/claude-code)
- [Run Codex on MIOSA Install the Codex CLI in a sandbox with streamed events.](/docs/build/codex)
- [Run Cursor agents on MIOSA Install the Cursor CLI agent and run it headless on isolated machines.](/docs/build/cursor)
- [Build a Windsurf-style agentic IDE An editor with an agent that edits across files and runs commands.](/docs/build/windsurf)
- [Build a GitHub Copilot-style coding agent An agent that takes an issue, works, and opens a PR.](/docs/build/github-copilot)
- [Run OpenHands on MIOSA Install the open-source software agent; the sandbox is its workspace.](/docs/build/openhands)
- [Run Cline on MIOSA The most-installed open-source coding agent, headless in a sandbox.](/docs/build/cline)
- [Build a coding-agent product Wrap a harness in your own branded product.](/docs/build/coding-agent-product)

### Autonomous agents

Agents with their own machine that plan and finish work.

- [Build a Manus-style agent A general agent with a desktop, browser, and files.](/docs/build/manus)
- [Build a Genspark-style agent A super-agent that plans and produces finished work.](/docs/build/genspark)

### Browser and computer-use agents

Build your own AI browser, platform or tool on MIOSA, or run an open-source browser agent.

- [Build your own browser agent Your model and loop, driving a sandbox browser or a full computer.](/docs/build/chatgpt-agent)
- [Build a Polar-style AI browser An AI browser that runs long tasks and scheduled workflows.](/docs/build/polar)
- [Run Browser Use on MIOSA Install the open-source library and let an agent drive a real browser.](/docs/build/browser-use)
- [Run Stagehand on MIOSA Install the framework and run reliable browser automations on a computer.](/docs/build/stagehand)

### AI chat and companions

Assistants and always-on companions.

- [Build a dots-style companion Always-on companions, each with its own cloud computer.](/docs/build/dots)
- [Build a Grok Bot-style chat app A team of named bots sharing one cloud computer.](/docs/build/grok-bot)
- [Build a Muse-style companion A personal companion that acts on your behalf across apps.](/docs/build/meta-muse)

- [Run OpenClaw on MIOSA Install the open-source assistant on a persistent computer that never sleeps.](/docs/build/openclaw)

### Answer engines

Research products that search, read, and answer with sources.

- [Build a Perplexity-style answer engine Search, read, and answer with citations.](/docs/build/perplexity)
- [Build a Comet-style agentic browser A browser that navigates and answers in place.](/docs/build/comet)
- [Build a You.com-style search and answer API An API your agents call to search and answer, with sources.](/docs/build/you-com)
- [Build a Phind-style answer engine Technical answers rendered as interactive mini-apps.](/docs/build/phind)
- [Build a deep-research-style agent A long-running research agent producing a report.](/docs/build/deep-research)

### Multi-agent

One request, many agents working in parallel.

- [Build an OpenSwarm-style multi-agent app An AI desktop built around running several agents in parallel.](/docs/build/openswarm)
- [Run Hermes Agent on MIOSA Install the open-source agent harness and run many tool-using agents.](/docs/build/hermes-agent)
- [Build an orchestrator that delegates One agent that plans, delegates to sub-agents and joins the result.](/docs/build/gemini-agent)

### Voice agents

Agents that talk and act on calls.

- [Build an ElevenLabs-style voice agent A voice agent that talks and takes real actions.](/docs/build/elevenlabs)
- [Build a Vapi-style voice agent Voice agents for phone and web.](/docs/build/vapi)
- [Build a Retell-style voice agent Phone agents that handle real calls.](/docs/build/retell)
- [Build a Bland-style phone agent Programmable phone agents at scale.](/docs/build/bland)
- [Run Pipecat on MIOSA Install the open-source voice pipeline from speech-to-text to text-to-speech.](/docs/build/pipecat)
- [Run LiveKit Agents on MIOSA The leading open-source realtime voice agent framework.](/docs/build/livekit-agents)

### AI design tools

Prompt to a designed UI or asset.

- [Build a prompt-to-UI design tool Prompt (and a design file) to a working, previewed UI.](/docs/build/figma-make)
- [Build a sketch-to-mockup tool A sketch or screenshot becomes editable UI code.](/docs/build/uizard)
- [Build a Magic-Patterns-style tool Generate UI components from a prompt.](/docs/build/magic-patterns)

### AI video and creative

Generate, edit, and produce media.

- [Build a video-generation app Generate and edit video on top of video-model APIs.](/docs/build/runway)
- [Build a text-to-video app Prompt to video through a video-model API.](/docs/build/sora)
- [Build an avatar-video app Script to talking-avatar video with TTS and lip-sync APIs.](/docs/build/heygen)
- [Build a Higgsfield-style video studio A multi-model studio: brief, steer camera and look, generate.](/docs/build/higgsfield)
- [Build a Gamma-style deck app Prompt or document to a polished, shareable deck or page.](/docs/build/gamma)
- [Build a Descript-style editor Edit video by editing the transcript.](/docs/build/descript)

### Vertical AI apps

Agents for a specific industry workflow.

- [Build a Fin-style support agent An AI support agent resolving customer tickets.](/docs/build/intercom-fin)
- [Build a Decagon-style support agent Resolve tickets across chat and email, with handoff.](/docs/build/decagon)
- [Build a Clay-style sales agent Research and enrich leads at scale.](/docs/build/clay)
- [Build a post-call analysis agent Turn call transcripts into sourced insights and next steps.](/docs/build/gong)
- [Build an OpenEvidence-style evidence engine Cited answers over a trusted corpus.](/docs/build/openevidence)

### Internal company apps

Build these for your own company: one organization, a workspace per team.

- [Build an internal Business OS MIOSA's own BusinessOS template, Apache 2.0.](/docs/build/business-os)
- [Build an internal AI workspace One place for your team's agents, apps, and data.](/docs/build/team-ai-workspace)
- [Build an ops and support copilot Triage tickets and run runbooks, with human approval.](/docs/build/ops-support-copilot)
- [Build an internal tools builder Prompt to a shipped dashboard behind your domain.](/docs/build/internal-tools-builder)
- [Build a knowledge-base agent Answer from the company docs with citations.](/docs/build/knowledge-base-agent)
- [Build an employee onboarding agent Walks a new hire through their first week.](/docs/build/employee-onboarding-agent)

Trademarks belong to their owners; these guides show how to build similar products on MIOSA. No affiliation or endorsement is implied.

> **Note: Same template, every guide**
>
> Each guide has the same shape: a **prompt builder**, **What you're building**, a
> **What you need on MIOSA** checklist with a create command per resource, an **architecture
> diagram**, six numbered steps (**create an account and API key → create the resources → wire
> the agent loop → preview → deploy → custom domain**), **costs and limits**, and **next steps**.

## Start with the platform

- [Platform builder guide](/docs/platform/overview): Organizations, workspaces, white-label, tenants, and billing.

pages.title: Build a Lovable-style app
pages.description: Lovable: Prompt a full-stack app, preview it live, publish it. Build it on MIOSA with the exact resources, steps and commands.
pages.markdown:
`~25 min` `TypeScript` `Python`

> **What you're building**: Prompt a full-stack app, preview it live, publish it.
>
> **Primitives you'll use**: Sandbox, Agent and harness, Deployment (Docker Host)

## What you're building

an AI app builder where users describe an app in chat and get a running full-stack web app with a live preview and one-click publish Modelled on Lovable, by Lovable.

A chat prompt goes to an agent that writes a web app (a React front end with backend integrations such as a database and auth), runs it, shows a live preview, lets the user keep iterating in chat, and publishes it to a hosted URL.

Primitives you'll use: Sandbox · Agent and harness · Deployment (App Engine)

- Describe an app in chat and get a working full-stack app
- Live preview that updates as the agent edits
- Iterate by chatting; fix build errors automatically
- Publish to a hosted URL, optionally on a custom domain

Source: [lovable.dev](https://lovable.dev/). Lovable is a trademark of its owner; this guide is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

## What you need on MIOSA

Each row is one thing to create before you start. The number matches the step that uses it.

1. Organization and API key - Scopes every call; a workspace key is all a worker needs. - `miosa api-key create app-key --preset agent` [Docs](/docs/platform/api-keys)
2. Sandbox - The isolated Linux workspace the agent writes code and runs commands in. - `miosa create app-box --template nextjs --wait` [Docs](/docs/develop/sandboxes)
3. A workspace per customer - Isolates each customer’s machines, deployments, and data as they onboard. - `miosa workspace create customer-1` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
4. Branding and white-label - Your name and slug on previews, deployments, and the desktop; customers never see MIOSA. - `miosa org` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
5. Usage metering and bill-to - Usage per customer, and which account pays for new machines. - `miosa org bill` [Docs](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing)
6. Agent and harness - Turns a prompt into work: pick the harness and model a run uses. - `miosa agent harnesses` [Docs](/docs/api-reference/agent-runs)
7. Deployment (App Engine) - Publishes the app to an immutable, versioned URL with rollback. - `miosa deploy create --from-sandbox app-box --name app --wait` [Docs](/docs/docker-host/overview)

## Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant P as Your product
  participant A as Agent
  participant S as MIOSA Sandbox
  participant D as MIOSA Deploy

  U->>P: describe the app to build
  P->>A: start a build task
  A->>S: create a project sandbox
  A->>S: write files, install, build
  S-->>P: stream stdout and file events
```

Harness: OSA is MIOSA's own harness and works with any model provider you connect, including your own model.

Each project is isolated in its own sandbox.

- One-step hosting

Each row is one thing to create before you start. The number matches the step that uses it.

1. Organization and API key - Scopes every call; a workspace key is all a worker needs. - `miosa api-key create app-key --preset agent` [Docs](/docs/platform/api-keys)
2. Sandbox - The isolated Linux workspace the agent writes code and runs commands in. - `miosa create app-box --template nextjs --wait` [Docs](/docs/develop/sandboxes)
3. A workspace per customer - Isolates each customer’s machines, deployments, and data as they onboard. - `miosa workspace create customer-1` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
4. Branding and white-label - Your name and slug on previews, deployments, and the desktop; customers never see MIOSA. - `miosa org` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
5. Usage metering and bill-to - Usage per customer, and which account pays for new machines. - `miosa org bill` [Docs](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant P as Your product
  participant A as Agent
  participant S as MIOSA Sandbox
  participant D as MIOSA Deploy

  U->>P: describe the app to build
  P->>A: start a build task
  A->>S: create a project sandbox
  A->>S: write files, install, build
  S-->>P: stream stdout and file events
  P->>S: start the dev server on port 3000
  S-->>P: preview URL for the user
  U->>P: ship it
  P->>D: publish from the sandbox
  D-->>P: public URL
```

## How it maps onto MIOSA

Each project is an isolated workspace -> one MIOSA sandbox per project

The agent writes and edits the code -> agent runs (`miosa prompt`, client.runs) streaming events against the project sandbox, files written inside it

Live preview while it builds -> a sandbox preview URL (`miosa preview create`)

Your control plane stores projects (id, owner, sandbox id, preview URL, deployment id, status), chat messages per project, and a version list (snapshot id, deployment version). The generated app's files live only in the project sandbox's /workspace.

Your organization is the platform; customers never get a MIOSA account, they sign into YOUR product. One workspace per customer, created as they onboard, isolates their machines, runs and data.

Harness: OSA is MIOSA's own harness and works with any model provider you connect, including your own model.

   ```bash
   miosa create base44-box --template nextjs --wait
   ```

   ```bash

   ```




One sandbox per active project is the cost driver: pause idle ones, destroy abandoned ones.

Prototype: keep it to one machine at the default size, skip replicas and custom hostnames you do not need, and delete everything when you are done.

Each customer is isolated in its own workspace and usage is metered against them.

Everything it created can be deleted with nothing left running.

Your control plane stores projects (id, owner, sandbox id, preview URL, deployment id, status), chat messages per project, and a version list (snapshot id, deployment version). The generated app's files live only in the project sandbox's /workspace.

Generated apps are stateless unless the user asks for data; add a per-project Postgres at that point.

## Auth and tenancy

Your organization is the platform; customers never get a MIOSA account, they sign into YOUR product. One workspace per customer, created as they onboard, isolates their machines, runs and data.

```bash
miosa workspace create anything-customer-1
```

Tag every machine and run with the customer id in `metadata`, and never query across customers. Meter usage per customer with GET /api/v1/usage and set who pays with PUT /api/v1/bill-to (/docs/platform/usage-and-billing).

## Agent loop

Harness: OSA is MIOSA's own harness and works with any model provider you connect, including your own model.

Model: Anthropic (Claude). Calls use my own provider key (`miosa connections add models`); MIOSA platform keys are never used.

Sessions: one chat per project or conversation, so the agent keeps its context. The first `miosa prompt` on a sandbox uses `--new-chat` (a chat id is printed); every later turn passes `--chat <chat-id>`. `--reuse chat` keeps one new machine per chat so files persist.

Streaming: follow a run with `miosa run follow <run-id>` or client.runs.streamEvents(run.id), and steer or stop it with `miosa run steer` and `miosa run interrupt`.

The harness works INSIDE the project sandbox: it writes files, runs the build and starts the dev server there. Do not build locally and upload the result.

When the build fails, feed the compiler output back as the next turn on the same chat ("fix the build") until it exits 0.

## Steps

1. Create one sandbox per project, inside the customer's workspace, named from the project id.
   ```bash
   miosa create anything-box --template nextjs --wait
   ```
   Check: The sandbox is running and `miosa exec` returns output.
2. Hand the user's prompt to the agent. It writes the files into /workspace, installs and builds.
   ```bash
   miosa prompt --sandbox anything-box --harness osa --model <anthropic-model-id> --chat <chat-id> "Build what the user asked for under /workspace; run npm install and npm run build; fix errors until it builds"
   ```
   Check: /workspace holds the app and `miosa exec anything-box -- npm run build` exits 0.
3. Start the app as a background process and open a preview the UI can embed.
   ```text
   sandbox.process.start("npm run dev", { name: "web", cwd: "/workspace" })
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa preview create anything-box 3000 --name web
   ```
   Check: The preview URL answers 200 and shows the app; it updates when the agent edits files.
4. Iterate: every follow-up message is another turn on the same chat. Snapshot before each change so the user can go back, and fork to compare two approaches.
   ```text
   sandbox.snapshots.create("before <change>")
   ```
   ```text
   sandbox.fork()
   ```
   Check: The previous version can be restored, and a fork leaves the original untouched.
5. Publish. A server-rendered app becomes a dynamic deployment; a static export publishes from /workspace/out.
   ```bash
   miosa deploy create --from-sandbox anything-box --name anything --dir /workspace --port 3000 --run-command "npm start" --wait
   ```
   Check: The deployment returns a public_url that answers, and it is a new immutable version.

## Limits and costs

Set an explicit `timeout_sec` (1h suits interactive building) and `idle_timeout_sec` so abandoned projects pause and stop billing; persistent sandboxes keep /workspace and installed dependencies.

Use a published template (nextjs) instead of reinstalling dependencies for every project.

One sandbox per active project is the cost driver: pause idle ones, destroy abandoned ones.

Prototype: keep it to one machine at the default size, skip replicas and custom hostnames you do not need, and delete everything when you are done.

## Acceptance checks

The app builds and the preview shows it.

Each project is isolated in its own sandbox.

The published URL answers and an earlier version can be restored.

Each customer is isolated in its own workspace and usage is metered against them.

Everything it created can be deleted with nothing left running.

pages.markdown:
`~25 min` `TypeScript` `Python`

> **What you're building**: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor: background agents in the cloud.
>
> **Primitives you'll use**: Sandbox, Agent and harness

## What you're building

background coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) running in the cloud instead of on a laptop Modelled on Cloud coding agents, by Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor and others.

A task is dispatched to an agent that clones the repo into an isolated machine, edits and tests it there, and returns events, files and a diff; many tasks run in parallel.

Primitives you'll use: Sandbox · Agent and harness

- Run an agent on a task in the background
- Many tasks in parallel, each isolated
- Stream progress and collect results
- A persistent workspace per developer or customer

Source: [/docs/api-reference/agent-runs](/docs/api-reference/agent-runs). Cloud coding agents is a trademark of Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor and others; this guide is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

## What you need on MIOSA

Each row is one thing to create before you start. The number matches the step that uses it.

1. Organization and API key - Scopes every call; a workspace key is all a worker needs. - `miosa api-key create app-key --preset agent` [Docs](/docs/platform/api-keys)
2. Sandbox - The isolated Linux workspace the agent writes code and runs commands in. - `miosa create app-box --template nextjs --wait` [Docs](/docs/develop/sandboxes)
3. A workspace per customer - Isolates each customer’s machines, deployments, and data as they onboard. - `miosa workspace create customer-1` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
4. Branding and white-label - Your name and slug on previews, deployments, and the desktop; customers never see MIOSA. - `miosa org` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
5. Usage metering and bill-to - Usage per customer, and which account pays for new machines. - `miosa org bill` [Docs](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing)
6. Agent and harness - Turns a prompt into work: pick the harness and model a run uses. - `miosa agent harnesses` [Docs](/docs/api-reference/agent-runs)

## Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant P as Your product
  participant S as Task sandbox
  participant A as Coding harness
  participant G as Git host

  U->>P: submit a task or an issue
  P->>S: create one sandbox per task
  P->>S: clone the repo, create a branch
  P->>A: dispatch the harness with the task
  A->>S: edit files, run the tests, commit
  S-->>P: events, diff and result files
  P->>G: push the branch and open a PR
  G-->>U: review the change
```

## How it maps onto MIOSA

A workspace the agent can break safely -> a MIOSA sandbox per task, with the repo cloned into /workspace

The agent edits files and runs commands -> agent runs (`miosa prompt`, client.runs) streaming events on that sandbox (`miosa prompt --sandbox ... --harness ...`)

Parallel tasks -> one sandbox per task or branch, sandbox snapshots and fork to try a second approach

Results you can review -> `miosa run files`, `miosa run outputs`, and the git diff inside the sandbox

## Data and storage

Keep a tasks table in your own datastore: task id, repo, branch, sandbox id, run id, status, result links, and the user or customer it belongs to. The code itself lives in the sandbox and in Git, not in your database.

Nothing else needs storage: Git is the system of record for the code.

## Auth and tenancy

Your organization is the platform; customers never get a MIOSA account, they sign into YOUR product. One workspace per customer, created as they onboard, isolates their machines, runs and data.

```bash
miosa workspace create run-agents-customer-1
```

Tag every machine and run with the customer id in `metadata`, and never query across customers. Meter usage per customer with GET /api/v1/usage and set who pays with PUT /api/v1/bill-to (/docs/platform/usage-and-billing).

## Agent loop

Harness: OSA is MIOSA's own harness and works with any model provider you connect, including your own model.

Model: Anthropic (Claude). Calls use my own provider key (`miosa connections add models`); MIOSA platform keys are never used.

Sessions: one chat per project or conversation, so the agent keeps its context. The first `miosa prompt` on a sandbox uses `--new-chat` (a chat id is printed); every later turn passes `--chat <chat-id>`. `--reuse chat` keeps one new machine per chat so files persist.

Streaming: follow a run with `miosa run follow <run-id>` or client.runs.streamEvents(run.id), and steer or stop it with `miosa run steer` and `miosa run interrupt`.

The harness runs headless INSIDE the task sandbox with the repo checked out. It edits files, runs the project's own commands and commits; you never apply its edits from outside.

Parallel sessions are separate sandboxes (and separate chats). Snapshot before a risky change and fork to try a second approach.

## Steps

1. Create one sandbox per task or branch so parallel tasks never share state.
   ```bash
   miosa create run-agents-task-1 --size medium --wait
   ```
   Check: The sandbox is running; two tasks have two sandboxes.
2. Clone the repository and create the task branch. Pass the Git token per exec or through the Secrets API; do not store it in the sandbox `env`.
   ```bash
   miosa exec run-agents-task-1 -- git clone <repo-url> /workspace/repo
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa exec run-agents-task-1 --cwd /workspace/repo -- git checkout -b task/<task-id>
   ```
   Check: The repo is in /workspace/repo on the task branch.
3. Dispatch the harness with the task.
   ```bash
   miosa prompt --sandbox run-agents-task-1 --harness osa --model <anthropic-model-id> --chat <chat-id> "Do the task; run the tests; commit your work"
   ```
   Check: `miosa run list --status running` shows the run and events start streaming.
4. Follow the run, and steer or stop it from your UI.
   ```bash
   miosa run follow <run-id>
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa run steer --sandbox run-agents-task-1 "also add tests"
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa run interrupt --sandbox run-agents-task-1
   ```
   Check: The UI shows live events; a steer lands on the next turn; interrupt stops the agent.
5. Verify independently of the agent: run the test command yourself.
   ```bash
   miosa exec run-agents-task-1 --cwd /workspace/repo -- npm test
   ```
   Check: Tests exit 0 in the sandbox, not just in the agent's summary.
6. Hand back the result: collect files and the diff, and push the branch if the task asks for it.
   ```bash
   miosa run files <run-id>
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa run download <run-id> <file-id> --output ./result
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa exec run-agents-task-1 --cwd /workspace/repo -- git push origin task/<task-id>
   ```
   Check: The diff is reviewable outside the sandbox and the run id is attached to it.
7. Close out. For one-shot tasks let MIOSA do it (`miosa prompt --new-machine ... --after-run destroy`); keep or snapshot the sandbox when the user may continue.
   Check: No orphaned sandboxes remain after the task is closed.

## Limits and costs

Set `--max-time` on every run so a stuck agent cannot run forever; use `--notify-email` or a webhook for long tasks.

Give the agent a token scoped to one repository, and only the permissions the task needs.

Parallel tasks multiply cost: cap concurrency per user or customer.

Prototype: keep it to one machine at the default size, skip replicas and custom hostnames you do not need, and delete everything when you are done.

## Acceptance checks

Two tasks run at the same time in two sandboxes without touching each other.

A finished task leaves a reviewable branch or diff and the run id.

Nothing was deployed or published: the deliverable is the diff.

Each customer is isolated in its own workspace and usage is metered against them.

Everything it created can be deleted with nothing left running.

## Next steps

- [Agent prompt builder Pick a product shape and hand the brief to your agent.](/docs/build)
- [Run coding agents Run Claude Code, Codex or Cursor in the cloud, or build a product on them.](/docs/build/run-agents)
- [Compare MIOSA How MIOSA compares to other sandbox and agent platforms.](/docs/compare)
- [What you can build Every product pattern MIOSA supports.](/docs/use-cases)

pages.title: Build a Windsurf-style agentic IDE
pages.description: Windsurf: An editor with an agent that edits across files and runs commands. Build it on MIOSA with the exact resources, steps and commands.
pages.markdown:
`~25 min` `TypeScript` `Python`

> **What you're building**: An editor with an agent that edits across files and runs commands.
>
> **Primitives you'll use**: Sandbox, Agent and harness

## What you're building

an agentic IDE where an agent edits code and runs commands alongside you Modelled on Windsurf, by Cognition.

Windsurf pairs an editor with an agent that plans multi-file changes and runs terminal commands; here the agents run against isolated machines.

Primitives you'll use: Sandbox · Agent and harness

- Agentic multi-file edits
- Runs terminal commands
- Keeps context across a session
- Review changes before accepting

Source: [windsurf.com](https://windsurf.com/). Windsurf is a trademark of Cognition; this guide is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

## What you need on MIOSA

Each row is one thing to create before you start. The number matches the step that uses it.

1. Organization and API key - Scopes every call; a workspace key is all a worker needs. - `miosa api-key create app-key --preset agent` [Docs](/docs/platform/api-keys)
2. Sandbox - The isolated Linux workspace the agent writes code and runs commands in. - `miosa create app-box --template nextjs --wait` [Docs](/docs/develop/sandboxes)
3. A workspace per customer - Isolates each customer’s machines, deployments, and data as they onboard. - `miosa workspace create customer-1` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
4. Branding and white-label - Your name and slug on previews, deployments, and the desktop; customers never see MIOSA. - `miosa org` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
5. Usage metering and bill-to - Usage per customer, and which account pays for new machines. - `miosa org bill` [Docs](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing)
6. Agent and harness - Turns a prompt into work: pick the harness and model a run uses. - `miosa agent harnesses` [Docs](/docs/api-reference/agent-runs)

## Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant P as Your product
  participant S as Task sandbox
  participant A as Coding harness
  participant G as Git host

  U->>P: submit a task or an issue
  P->>S: create one sandbox per task
  P->>S: clone the repo, create a branch
  P->>A: dispatch the harness with the task
  A->>S: edit files, run the tests, commit
  S-->>P: events, diff and result files
  P->>G: push the branch and open a PR
  G-->>U: review the change
```

## How it maps onto MIOSA

A workspace the agent can break safely -> a MIOSA sandbox per task, with the repo cloned into /workspace

The agent edits files and runs commands -> agent runs (`miosa prompt`, client.runs) streaming events on that sandbox (`miosa prompt --sandbox ... --harness ...`)

Parallel tasks -> one sandbox per task or branch, sandbox snapshots and fork to try a second approach

Results you can review -> `miosa run files`, `miosa run outputs`, and the git diff inside the sandbox

## Data and storage

Keep a tasks table in your own datastore: task id, repo, branch, sandbox id, run id, status, result links, and the user or customer it belongs to. The code itself lives in the sandbox and in Git, not in your database.

Nothing else needs storage: Git is the system of record for the code.

## Auth and tenancy

Your organization is the platform; customers never get a MIOSA account, they sign into YOUR product. One workspace per customer, created as they onboard, isolates their machines, runs and data.

```bash
miosa workspace create windsurf-customer-1
```

Tag every machine and run with the customer id in `metadata`, and never query across customers. Meter usage per customer with GET /api/v1/usage and set who pays with PUT /api/v1/bill-to (/docs/platform/usage-and-billing).

## Agent loop

Harness: OSA is MIOSA's own harness and works with any model provider you connect, including your own model.

Model: Anthropic (Claude). Calls use my own provider key (`miosa connections add models`); MIOSA platform keys are never used.

Sessions: one chat per project or conversation, so the agent keeps its context. The first `miosa prompt` on a sandbox uses `--new-chat` (a chat id is printed); every later turn passes `--chat <chat-id>`. `--reuse chat` keeps one new machine per chat so files persist.

Streaming: follow a run with `miosa run follow <run-id>` or client.runs.streamEvents(run.id), and steer or stop it with `miosa run steer` and `miosa run interrupt`.

The harness runs headless INSIDE the task sandbox with the repo checked out. It edits files, runs the project's own commands and commits; you never apply its edits from outside.

Parallel sessions are separate sandboxes (and separate chats). Snapshot before a risky change and fork to try a second approach.

## Steps

1. Create one sandbox per task or branch so parallel tasks never share state.
   ```bash
   miosa create windsurf-task-1 --size medium --wait
   ```
   Check: The sandbox is running; two tasks have two sandboxes.
2. Clone the repository and create the task branch. Pass the Git token per exec or through the Secrets API; do not store it in the sandbox `env`.
   ```bash
   miosa exec windsurf-task-1 -- git clone <repo-url> /workspace/repo
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa exec windsurf-task-1 --cwd /workspace/repo -- git checkout -b task/<task-id>
   ```
   Check: The repo is in /workspace/repo on the task branch.
3. Dispatch the harness with the task.
   ```bash
   miosa prompt --sandbox windsurf-task-1 --harness osa --model <anthropic-model-id> --chat <chat-id> "Do the task; run the tests; commit your work"
   ```
   Check: `miosa run list --status running` shows the run and events start streaming.
4. Follow the run, and steer or stop it from your UI.
   ```bash
   miosa run follow <run-id>
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa run steer --sandbox windsurf-task-1 "also add tests"
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa run interrupt --sandbox windsurf-task-1
   ```
   Check: The UI shows live events; a steer lands on the next turn; interrupt stops the agent.
5. Verify independently of the agent: run the test command yourself.
   ```bash
   miosa exec windsurf-task-1 --cwd /workspace/repo -- npm test
   ```
   Check: Tests exit 0 in the sandbox, not just in the agent's summary.
6. Hand back the result: collect files and the diff, and push the branch if the task asks for it.
   ```bash
   miosa run files <run-id>
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa run download <run-id> <file-id> --output ./result
   ```
   ```bash
   miosa exec windsurf-task-1 --cwd /workspace/repo -- git push origin task/<task-id>
   ```
   Check: The diff is reviewable outside the sandbox and the run id is attached to it.
7. Close out. For one-shot tasks let MIOSA do it (`miosa prompt --new-machine ... --after-run destroy`); keep or snapshot the sandbox when the user may continue.
   Check: No orphaned sandboxes remain after the task is closed.

## Limits and costs

Set `--max-time` on every run so a stuck agent cannot run forever; use `--notify-email` or a webhook for long tasks.

Give the agent a token scoped to one repository, and only the permissions the task needs.

Parallel tasks multiply cost: cap concurrency per user or customer.

Prototype: keep it to one machine at the default size, skip replicas and custom hostnames you do not need, and delete everything when you are done.

## Acceptance checks

Two tasks run at the same time in two sandboxes without touching each other.

A finished task leaves a reviewable branch or diff and the run id.

Nothing was deployed or published: the deliverable is the diff.

Each customer is isolated in its own workspace and usage is metered against them.

Everything it created can be deleted with nothing left running.

## Next steps

- [Agent prompt builder Pick a product shape and hand the brief to your agent.](/docs/build)
- [Run coding agents Run Claude Code, Codex or Cursor in the cloud, or build a product on them.](/docs/build/run-agents)
- [Compare MIOSA How MIOSA compares to other sandbox and agent platforms.](/docs/compare)
- [What you can build Every product pattern MIOSA supports.](/docs/use-cases)

pages.description: OpenHands: Install the open-source software agent; the sandbox is its workspace. Install and run it on a MIOSA sandbox or computer, then wrap it for your team or your customers.
pages.markdown:
`~15 min` `TypeScript` `Python`

> **What you're building**: Install the open-source software agent; the sandbox is its workspace.
>
> **Primitives you'll use**: Sandbox

## What you're building

an open-source software-engineering agent that works in a sandboxed workspace Modelled on OpenHands, by All Hands AI.

OpenHands runs an agent loop that edits files, runs commands and browses inside a sandboxed runtime, driven by a task description.

Primitives you'll use: Sandbox

- Open-source SWE agent
- Sandboxed runtime for commands and files
- Works on GitHub issues and tasks
- Bring your own model

You install and **run the real OpenHands** on MIOSA. Read the official docs first: [github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands). Every install command below comes from them; if the docs and this guide disagree, the docs win. OpenHands is open source (the Agent Canvas front end and agent server).

## What you need on MIOSA

Each row is one thing to create before you start. The number matches the step that uses it.

1. Organization and API key - Scopes every call; a workspace key is all a worker needs. - `miosa api-key create app-key --preset agent` [Docs](/docs/platform/api-keys)
2. Sandbox - The isolated Linux workspace the agent writes code and runs commands in. - `miosa create app-box --template nextjs --wait` [Docs](/docs/develop/sandboxes)
3. A workspace per customer - Isolates each customer’s machines, deployments, and data as they onboard. - `miosa workspace create customer-1` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
4. Branding and white-label - Your name and slug on previews, deployments, and the desktop; customers never see MIOSA. - `miosa org` [Docs](/docs/platform/white-label)
5. Usage metering and bill-to - Usage per customer, and which account pays for new machines. - `miosa org bill` [Docs](/docs/platform/usage-and-billing)

## Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as You
  participant M as MIOSA Sandbox
  participant P as Model provider
  participant D as MIOSA Deploy

  U->>M: install the tool from its official docs
  M->>P: calls with your own provider key
  U->>M: run a real task
  M-->>U: output, files and a preview URL
  U->>D: publish it for your team or your customers
```

## How it runs on MIOSA

Where it runs -> a MIOSA sandbox (an isolated Linux workspace)

State and files -> State lives under `~/.openhands`; a persistent sandbox keeps it across pauses. Keep project folders under /workspace.

Model -> your own provider key, never a MIOSA platform key

Its web port 8000 -> a MIOSA preview URL (`miosa preview create`)

Your customers -> one workspace each, isolated from each other

## Auth and tenancy

Your organization is the platform; customers never get a MIOSA account, they sign into YOUR product. One workspace per customer, created as they onboard, isolates their machines, runs and data.

```bash
miosa workspace create openhands-customer-1
```

Tag every machine and run with the customer id in `metadata`, and never query across customers. Meter usage per customer with GET /api/v1/usage and set who pays with PUT /api/v1/bill-to (/docs/platform/usage-and-billing).

## Install OpenHands

Run these inside the sandbox (for example `miosa exec openhands-task-1 -- bash -lc '<command>'`), in order. The commands are from the official docs.

```bash
node --version   # Node.js 24 or later is required
```

```text
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

```bash
npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas
```

Check: the install finishes without errors; the next sections configure and start it.

## Configure

Open the UI, add an LLM profile in Settings, and paste your own provider key. The MIOSA sandbox is already the isolation boundary, so use the "without a Docker sandbox" mode the README describes.

Model: Anthropic (Claude). Calls use my own provider key (entered in the tool's own setup); MIOSA platform keys are never used.

## Run it

Start it and prove it works.

```text
agent-canvas
```

Check: the tool starts without errors and responds.

## Persistence and access

State lives under `~/.openhands`; a persistent sandbox keeps it across pauses. Keep project folders under /workspace.

It listens on port 8000. Run it as a background process so it outlives your shell, then open a preview:

```bash
miosa preview create openhands-task-1 8000 --name web
```

Check: the preview URL answers, and still answers after the machine pauses and resumes (previews wake it on request).

## Make it a product

Run one OpenHands sandbox per customer workspace and put your own auth in front of the preview URL; never expose an unauthenticated agent server.

## Limits and costs

Pin the version you tested and update deliberately; these tools change quickly.

Give the tool only the credentials it needs, as secrets, not baked into files.

Prototype: keep it to one machine at the default size, skip replicas and custom hostnames you do not need, and delete everything when you are done.

## Acceptance checks

OpenHands runs on a MIOSA sandbox and answers a real task.

State survives a pause and resume.

Each customer has its own workspace and its own instance; nothing is shared between them.

Everything it created can be deleted with nothing left running.
